title: Asymptotically sharp acquisition threshold for few-copy decoding

claims.statement: For every N >= 2 and every s modulo N, the threshold-controlled Grover phase decoder in proof.md uses n=ceil(log2 N) and acquires exactly k in {n,n+1}, determined by its public rational moment and Poisson guard. It recovers all of s with unconditional probability greater than 2/3 from independent ideal copies. The same configuration jointly has branchwise total charged work O(2^(n/2) n^2 (1+log2 log2(n+2)) b^2) for b=floor(max(1,floor(log2 n))^(1/128)), hence the supported envelope O(2^(n/2) n^2 (log2 n)^(1/8)), with growth index exactly 1.

It recovers all of s with unconditional probability greater than 2/3 from independent ideal copies. The same configuration jointly has peak allocated classical space O(n^2) bits on every branch, with growth index exactly 0.

For every N >= 2 and every s modulo N, the threshold-controlled Grover phase decoder in proof.md uses n=ceil(log2 N) and acquires exactly k in {n,n+1}, determined by its public rational moment and Poisson guard. It recovers all of s with unconditional probability greater than 2/3 from independent ideal copies. The same configuration jointly has acquisition count exactly the selected k on every branch, which is O(n) and has growth index exactly 0. Along any sequence with n tending to infinity and 2^n/N converging to a value other than the unique threshold specified in proof.md, this count is eventually the minimum possible count for worst-secret success at least 2/3.

For every N >= 2 and every s modulo N, the threshold-controlled Grover phase decoder in proof.md uses n=ceil(log2 N) and acquires exactly k in {n,n+1}, determined by its public rational moment and Poisson guard. It recovers all of s with unconditional probability greater than 2/3 from independent ideal copies. The same configuration jointly has guaranteed malformed fraction epsilon(n)=0 under the independent ideal-copy model.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
